name: Pritzker Group Venture Capital
identity_check: Pritzker Group Venture Capital (PGVC) is the technology venture arm of Pritzker Group, the Chicago investment firm led by Tony and J.B. Pritzker; it was called New World Ventures until October 2013 (Built In / PE Hub). Its pages sat under pritzkergroup.com/venture-capital/ (Internet Archive captures up to 2025-11-29, footer listing it beside Pritzker Group Private Capital and Pritzker Group Asset Management). On 2026-10-30 that path returns 404 and pritzkergroup.com is a one-page site for a 'family-backed investment firm' with no venture section; the LinkedIn company page (Chicago, 'Helping entrepreneurs achieve greatness') still links to the dead path. No new name found: SNAK Venture Partners (snak.vc) is a separate seed fund for marketplaces run by former PGVC partners Adam Koopersmith and Sonia Nagar, which lists PGVC deals only as their prior investments. Not Pritzker Group Private Capital (the group's private-equity arm) and not PSP Partners (a separate Pritzker vehicle that co-invested in Ocient's 2021 round). Type set to family_office: PGVC invests Pritzker family capital through an evergreen vehicle with no outside LPs. Status set to inactive as a judgement (see conflicts): the venture site is gone, news stops in May 2024, two of three listed investment partners left, and the latest round naming PGVC that was found is December 2023.

thesis_text.value: Venture arm investing the Pritzker family's own capital through an evergreen vehicle with no outside LPs, so no fixed exit timeline. Series A is the sweet spot, with selective seed and opportunistic follow-on checks, invested US-wide. Themes are marketplaces and vertical SaaS for industries slow to adopt technology, backed by Fortune 1000 relationships.

open_items: Funds: none recorded. PGVC calls itself an evergreen fund with no LPs; Chris Girgenti's bio says he led capital formation for seven technology venture funds, but no page gives their names, sizes or dates.

No round naming PGVC was found from the last 24 months (Nov 2024 to Oct 2026); the latest found is Machinery Partner's Series A (Dec 2023). Ocient's March 2024 Series B extension (reposted on PGVC's news page) says only 'all prior major investors', so it is not recorded.

Castelion's $350M Series B (Dec 2025): a search result (Seedtable) lists 'Pritzker Group' as a participant, but the Built In and Tectonic Defense articles name no Pritzker entity. Not verified, not recorded.
application_url: none found; the archived contact page lists only the Chicago and Los Angeles offices, with no pitch form.
accepts_cold_inbound, requires_us_entity and invests_in_indian_founders are unknown; the firm says only that it invests 'nationwide' (US).
portfolio_count_reported: no number is stated. The archived portfolio page (2025-07-23) lists 108 companies (42 active, 66 exited); that is a count, not a reported figure.
website: LinkedIn still points to https://www.pritzkergroup.com/venture-capital/, which returns 404 on 2026-10-30; the parent domain is recorded instead.

Current team unconfirmed: the last team capture (2025-01-16) lists Chris Girgenti, Adam Koopersmith, Sonia Nagar and operating partner Carter Cast (consumer/retail background, not recorded). Earlier industrial-deal contacts (Ty Findley on Plus One 2018, Peter Liu on Apprentice 2018) are not on the 2025 page and are not recorded.
Founding year differs: LinkedIn says 2002; the 2013 Built In article says New World Ventures was founded 18 years earlier (about 1995). Not a schema field.

A Crain's Currency headline (search result only; page returned 403) mentions a Pritzker Organization family office launching a $190M venture fund called '53'. That looks like a different Pritzker family vehicle and was not read.
Augury's 2017 Series B: the VC News Daily table lists 'Pritzker Private Capital', probably a mislabel of PGVC. The article was not read, so the round is not recorded.
